## AJ — CPG / Consumer Goods Strategy

### AJ.1 — CPG Portfolio & Brand Architecture

**AJ.1.01 — CPG Portfolio and Brand Architecture Operating Model for operating signal**
*Summary:* An operating model pattern for cpg portfolio & brand architecture that explains how the operating signal shapes retail performance beyond generic channel or product analysis.
*Mechanism:* In practice, the retailer translates cpg portfolio & brand architecture into governance cadence, accountable owners, escalation paths, and cross-functional rituals; the useful artifact is a decision table that separates enterprise rules from cluster, category, channel, and partner exceptions.
*Decision relevance:* CXOs use this pattern during seasonal reset to decide whether a modernization, sourcing, AI, growth, margin, or resilience initiative has enough economic proof to scale across banners and channels.
*Pitfalls:* The common failure mode is treating vendor tooling as a strategy instead of an operating-model change; the mitigation is to force a before/after control, owner, metric grain, and exception path before funding the next tranche.
*Industry exemplars:* European grocery and hard-discount tiers typically expose this pattern through anonymized peer ranges such as basis-point margin movement, conversion lift, shrink movement, labor minutes per transaction, inventory turns, service-level deltas, or repeat-rate movement rather than through a single brand anecdote.
*Cross-references:* AJ.1.02; retail-v1:AJ; AJ.1; operating-model

**AJ.1.02 — CPG Portfolio and Brand Architecture Unit Economics for economic driver**
*Summary:* A unit economics pattern for cpg portfolio & brand architecture that explains how the role of economic driver shapes retail performance beyond generic channel or product analysis.
*Mechanism:* In practice, the retailer translates cpg portfolio & brand architecture into margin, cost-to-serve, working capital, and customer lifetime value tradeoffs; the useful artifact is a decision table that separates enterprise rules from cluster, category, channel, and partner exceptions.
*Decision relevance:* CXOs use this pattern during weekly operating review to decide whether a modernization, sourcing, AI, growth, margin, or resilience initiative has enough economic proof to scale across banners and channels.
*Pitfalls:* The common failure mode is optimizing the visible KPI while moving cost, inventory, labor, or risk elsewhere; the mitigation is to force a before/after control, owner, metric grain, and exception path before funding the next tranche.
*Industry exemplars:* specialty apparel and beauty leaders typically expose this pattern through anonymized peer ranges such as basis-point margin movement, conversion lift, shrink movement, labor minutes per transaction, inventory turns, service-level deltas, or repeat-rate movement rather than through a single brand anecdote.
*Cross-references:* AJ.1.01, AJ.1.03; retail-v1:AJ; AJ.1; unit-economics

*Mechanism:* In practice, the retailer translates dtc unit economics into governance cadence, accountable owners, escalation paths, and cross-functional rituals; the useful artifact is a decision table that separates enterprise rules from cluster, category, channel, and partner exceptions.
*Decision relevance:* CXOs use this pattern during seasonal reset to decide whether a modernization, sourcing, AI, growth, margin, or resilience initiative has enough economic proof to scale across banners and channels.
*Pitfalls:* The common failure mode is treating vendor tooling as a strategy instead of an operating-model change; the mitigation is to force a before/after control, owner, metric grain, and exception path before funding the next tranche.
*Industry exemplars:* European grocery and hard-discount tiers typically expose this pattern through anonymized peer ranges such as basis-point margin movement, conversion lift, shrink movement, labor minutes per transaction, inventory turns, service-level deltas, or repeat-rate movement rather than through a single brand anecdote.
*Cross-references:* AQ.3.02; retail-v1:AQ; AQ.3; operating-model

*Mechanism:* In practice, the retailer translates retail p&l structure into SOPs, exception paths, control points, and field or digital auditability; the useful artifact is a decision table that separates enterprise rules from cluster, category, channel, and partner exceptions.
*Decision relevance:* CXOs use this pattern during seasonal reset to decide whether a modernization, sourcing, AI, growth, margin, or resilience initiative has enough economic proof to scale across banners and channels.
*Pitfalls:* The common failure mode is confusing short-run sales lift with durable margin, loyalty, or customer lifetime value; the mitigation is to force a before/after control, owner, metric grain, and exception path before funding the next tranche.
*Industry exemplars:* US3 mass-market retailers typically expose this pattern through anonymized peer ranges such as basis-point margin movement, conversion lift, shrink movement, labor minutes per transaction, inventory turns, service-level deltas, or repeat-rate movement rather than through a single brand anecdote.

*Mechanism:* In practice, the retailer translates retail m&a strategy into margin, cost-to-serve, working capital, and customer lifetime value tradeoffs; the useful artifact is a decision table that separates enterprise rules from cluster, category, channel, and partner exceptions.
*Decision relevance:* CXOs use this pattern during weekly operating review to decide whether a modernization, sourcing, AI, growth, margin, or resilience initiative has enough economic proof to scale across banners and channels.
*Pitfalls:* The common failure mode is optimizing the visible KPI while moving cost, inventory, labor, or risk elsewhere; the mitigation is to force a before/after control, owner, metric grain, and exception path before funding the next tranche.
*Industry exemplars:* specialty apparel and beauty leaders typically expose this pattern through anonymized peer ranges such as basis-point margin movement, conversion lift, shrink movement, labor minutes per transaction, inventory turns, service-level deltas, or repeat-rate movement rather than through a single brand anecdote.
*Cross-references:* AZ.1.01, AZ.1.03; retail-v1:AZ; AZ.1; unit-economics
